The proof was generated in conversation with ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; the authors provided high-level guidance in several rounds of prompting, followed by manual checking and rewriting of the proof.
item.dc:creator: Dylan J. Altschuler, Konstantin Tikhomirov

item.title: Rigorous Low-Degree Implications for Planted Subgraph Detection: Noise and Treewidth
item.description: arXiv:2608.06279v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The low-degree method predicts computational thresholds by asking whether low-degree polynomials can distinguish a planted distribution from a null one. Recent counterexamples by Buhai, Hsieh, Jain, and Kothari (FOCS 2025) and Mao (2026) show that low-degree indistinguishability does not, in general, rule out efficient algorithms, even on noisy inputs. Hsieh, Kane, Kothari, Li, Mohanty, and Tiegel (STOC 2026) asked what it does imply, and showed that for permutation-invariant distributions on $\{0,1\}^n$, low-degree indistinguishability from the uniform distribution implies statistical indistinguishability after noise. In this work, we study the same question for planted subgraphs in sparse random graphs. Let $Q_n=G(n,c/n)$, and let $P_n$ be obtained by planting a uniformly random copy of a deterministic graph $\Gamma_n$ into an independent sample from $Q_n$. In the supercritical regime $c>1$, we show that if $P_n$ is degree-$D_n$ indistinguishable from $Q_n$ and the treewidth of $\Gamma_n$ is $o(D_n/\log n)$, then a noisy version of $P_n$ is asymptotically indistinguishable from $Q_n$. In the critical and subcritical regimes $0<c\le 1$, we obtain the same conclusion without any treewidth assumption, provided $D_n=\omega(\log n)$. Our proof has two main ingredients. First, we identify the subgraph-count and automorphism factors in the Fourier expansion with counts of isomorphism triples. Second, we cut a tree decomposition of $\Gamma_n$ into subtrees, which splits each large Fourier support into low-degree pieces that meet at only a few interface vertices, and we use noise to absorb the cost of reassembling them. At and below criticality, we use the low-degree assumption to rule out short cycles and noise to destroy the remaining long ones.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Chen, Shuangping Li

item.title: Universality in random graphs via optimal linking systems: trees and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2608.06358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a framework for proving universality results in sparse random graphs. As a first application, we show that there exists an absolute constant $C>1$ such that, with high probability, for every fixed constant $\Delta$, the binomial random graph $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains every $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. This answers a question of Montgomery (Advances in Mathematics, 2019). We also determine, for every $p$ satisfying $C\ln n/n\leq p=n^{-1+o(1)}$, the minimum girth $\ell$ (up to an absolute multiplicative constant) for which with high probability $G(n,p)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $\Omega(\ell)$. In particular, with high probability $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $C\ln n/\ln\ln n$, which is optimal up to a constant factor. This extends an earlier result of Ferber, Kronenberg, and Luh (Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, 2019) and significantly improves a corollary of a deep result of Kahn, Lubetzky, and Wormald (Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, 2017). One of the key ingredients in the proofs is establishing the optimal depth of linking systems in sparse random graphs.
item.dc:creator: Asaf Cohen Antonir, Lyuben Lichev, Maksim Zhukovskii

item.title: The $\beta=2$ partition function of Dirichlet $L$-functions and typical maxima
item.description: arXiv:2608.09906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $\beta=2$ partition function $\int_{|h| \leq \log ^{\theta} q/2}|L(1/2+ih,\chi)|^2dh$ for typical Dirichlet characters modulo a large prime $q$ and $\theta \in (-1/3,0]$ motivated by a $q$-analogue of the Saksman--Webb conjectures. When $\theta <0$, we use an extension of Harper's randomisation argument with different localisations to recover moment upper bounds consistent with the critical normalisation predicted there. As an application, we prove that for $q(1-o(1))$ Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ with $U(q) \to \infty$, $$\max_{|h| \leq 1/2}|L(1/2+ih,\chi)|\ll \frac{e^{U(q)}\log q\log_3 q(\log_4 q)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 q)^{3/4}},$$ establishing an upper bound matching the predictions of the $q$-analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating conjectures up to second order. Our proofs adapt Harper's argument in \cite{harper2019partition}.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Atherfold

item.title: The Wave Kinetic Theory for Quasilinear MMT Equation
item.description:
arXiv:2608.22710v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional quasilinear Majda--McLaughlin--Tabak (MMT) equation on a large torus $[0,L]$:  egin{align*} i \partial_t u +2\pi|

We consider Gaussian random initial data and work in the joint limit $L	o\infty$ with $\alpha=\lambda^2L^{-1}	o0$. The quasilinear structure leads to unavoidable derivative loss, which prevents the direct construction of solutions via iteration of the Duhamel formula. For $\sigma\in(1,2]$, we prove that, with high probability, solutions exist up to time scales ${T} \sim\alpha^{-{ rac43}+} \wedge \alpha^{- rac1{\sigma/2- eta}+}$, and that only trivial four-wave resonances occur, leading to a degenerate wave kinetic equation. item.dc:creator: Huaxiang L\"u

item.title: A Spectral Local-to-Global Principle for Spin Systems on Graphs with Girth At Least Five
item.description: arXiv:2608.25491v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is proved that, for every $\delta \in (0,1)$, the Glauber dynamics for the uniform distribution on proper $q$-colorings is rapidly mixing when $q \geq (1+\delta)\Delta$ and the underlying graph has girth at least $5$ and maximum degree $\Delta = \Omega_\delta(1)$. This result also extends to general multi-spin systems satisfying a $\textit{local spectral contraction}$ condition, including the anti-ferromagnetic Potts model with $q\geq (1+\delta)(1-\beta)\Delta$. These results are achieved by a new spectral local-to-global principle on graphs with girth at least five for general multi-spin systems, and a novel Fourier analysis for Glauber dynamics on a star. The main ideas behind all the proofs were developed through several rounds of interaction with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

item.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
item.description: arXiv:2609.38044v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(\pi_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.
item.dc:creator: Qian Chen, Jingcheng Liu, Minglong Qin, Leonard J. Schulman, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao

item.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.06724v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) for approximately counting and uniformly sampling common bases of two matroids given by their independence oracles. Moreover, our algorithms generalize far beyond this to Hadamard products of two probability measures on the Boolean cube satisfying a simple nonnegative curvature condition. These algorithmic primitives have myriad applications in statistical physics, polyhedral combinatorics, the theory of quantum many-body systems, and beyond. The central difficulty is that the hard constraints imposed by the two input matroids (or the two input measures, more generally) obstruct traditional approaches based on local Markov chains. Relaxing these constraints can restore rapid mixing, but configurations that satisfy the original hard constraints may become exponentially rare if this is done na\"ively. Our main contribution is a novel approach for approximate counting that marries Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with convex programming to overcome these obstacles: - We relax the intersection by imposing an overlap penalty on the product measure formed by the two input measures. We prove, via an integrated Bochner-type method, that this "soft intersection" satisfies a Poincar\'e Inequality uniformly over all external fields. - We use samples from the relaxed distribution to solve a dual maximum entropy convex program inspired by the Gurvits capacity. This program reweights the soft intersection measure using external fields to boost the aggregate probability of configurations satisfying the hard intersection constraint, without changing their relative weights. We bound the success probability directly using the uniform Poincar\'e Inequality and smallness of the gradient norm. AI Disclosure: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra and GPT-6 Astra Ultra were heavily used to develop the ideas in this paper.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

item.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.08701v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the probability that Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting on $n \times n$ Gaussian random matrices has growth $\rho$ is at least inverse quasi-polynomial: $\Omega\left(\exp\left(-c \log^2 \left(\frac{\rho}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\log(n)\right)\right)$ for some constant $c > 0$. In particular, the probability of growth $\rho \ge n^{1/2 + \epsilon}$ is at least $\exp(- O (\epsilon^2 \log^3 (n) ))$. This lower bound breaks standard conjectures in the smoothed and average-case analysis of Gaussian elimination. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first non-trivial lower bound on the probability of large growth for Gaussian random matrices.
item.dc:creator: Daniel A. Spielman, Xifan Yu

item.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.16169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We answer, in the trace metric, a question of Kowalski and Untrau on Wasserstein distances of all orders between the distribution $\mu_q$ of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and the Sato-Tate law $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$: we prove bounds for every order $s$ and show that their exponents are optimal for Katz-type moment bounds. In the trace metric we prove $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll_s q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s<3$, $W_3\ll q^{-1/3}(\log q)^{1/3}$, $W_s\ll_s q^{-1/4-1/(4s)}$ for $3<s<\infty$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/4}$. In the angle metric we obtain bounds of every order, including $W_2\le 7q^{-1/3}$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/6}$. These estimates follow from a general theorem for probability measures satisfying Katz-type Chebyshev moment bounds. Its proof combines an edge-sensitive discrepancy estimate with a new level-set bound for the distribution function and a quantile-displacement argument. We construct measures showing that the resulting exponents cannot in general be improved using moment bounds of this type alone, in the trace metric and in the angle metric for $s\le 2$ and $s\ge 6$ (up to logarithms); these constructions do not assert optimality for the Kloosterman measures themselves. A sharp comparison between Wasserstein distances and the Kolmogorov distance for the Sato-Tate law exhibits the same transition at $s=3$. Finally, using the exact third moment, we prove $W_1(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})>q^{-1/2}/10$ when $3\nmid q$.
item.dc:creator: Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator with bounded nonconstant iid potential, we prove a unit-intensity Poisson limit for local eigenvalues unfolded by the integrated density of states. The limit holds at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. In particular, it holds for Bernoulli potentials at every fixed nonzero coupling. The proof uses auxiliary phase functions built from inverse stationary measures to obtain an exact IDS drift. Projective contraction then yields exponential crossing times, and a spatial subdivision argument gives independent Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows. At energies where the IDS has a finite positive derivative, the usual linear rescaling gives the same limit.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Bounded Error: Adaptive Reconstruction and Entropy bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35933v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study compression of real-valued stationary sources under a deterministic error bound: every sample must be reconstructed within a prescribed tolerance $\varepsilon$ on every input sequence. Reconstructions are causal, depending only on present and past inputs. Rates are measured by the entropy of the quantizer output, which block entropy coding can approach, and compared with the minimum rate of unrestricted block quantization under the same error constraint. A uniform scalar quantizer with cells of width $2\varepsilon$ is within one bit per sample of this minimum whenever finite-entropy scalar quantization is possible, without density, independence, or mixing assumptions. Under entropy and Sobolev regularity conditions, the gap is at most $2\mathcal{J}\varepsilon^2/(\pi^2\ln 2)$, where $\mathcal{J}$ is the asymptotic Fisher information per sample. Thus the cost of causal reconstruction vanishes at a quadratic rate as the tolerance decreases. A uniform grid, however, cannot adapt to the source. We construct an adaptive quantizer whose encoder and decoder maintain a common finite set of reconstruction values, updated from the transmitted symbols alone; suitable initialization reproduces any uniform grid. When its initial values are at least $\varepsilon$ apart, its rate is within two bits per sample of the minimum for every such source. For sources uniform within separated intervals of width $2\varepsilon$, storing the interval centers attains the minimum and its Shannon lower bound. Such configurations can outperform every uniform grid of the same cell width: over sources with well-separated intervals, the best uniform grid's worst-case excess rate is $1/(2\ln 2)\approx 0.72$ bit per sample.
item.dc:creator: Rama Cont, Massoud Heidari

item.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.40510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $\beta=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$\alpha < \alpha_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. As a key intermediate step, we establish the pointwise equivalence, away from the threshold, of three notions of replica symmetry: geometric (averaged pairwise correlation decay), thermodynamic (convergence to the Bethe free-energy prediction), and variational (nonpositivity of the Bethe functional). To establish zero-freeness, we develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, lifting classical small subgraph conditioning to random holomorphic functions to control short-cycle fluctuations. We also use variational replica symmetry to obtain exponential planted overlap concentration. This enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.
item.dc:creator: Zejia Chen, Chunyang Wang, Xinyuan Zhang

item.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40562v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-Majority, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-Majority achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results. For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $$\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-Majority that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration. When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds. We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.
item.dc:creator: Francesco d'Amore, Joel Rybicki, Nobutaka Shimizu, Takeharu Shiraga, Robin Vacus

item.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{T}_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.
